headlines.text: That Saturday in 2025, the AEW Women's World Title had a new owner by the end of the night as Toni Storm vs. Mariah May battled it out, appearing on Grand Slam: Australia, rated 7.13 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle ? ending the champion's reign at 8 defenses. Storm reclaimed the AEW Women's World Championship from May with a small package counter, becoming a four-time champion in front of a hometown Brisbane crowd.

2021 brought us this moment: VENY kicked off their AEW journey against Emi Sakura, appearing on AEW Women's World Title Tournament, rated 8.11 ? an excellent showing. A close first-round match in AEW's first-ever Women's World Title Eliminator Tournament ? Veny nearly pulled off a shock finish before Emi Sakura, complete with a Freddie Mercury-tribute mustache, escaped with a tiger driver, capped by a mid-air slap for good measure.
Back on this day in 2023, Preston Vance returned to the fold after just under 2 months away, appearing on Dynamite.

secondaries.text: Back on this day in 2021, Rin Kadokura wasted no time making an impression, debuting right in the main event against Aja Kong, appearing on AEW Women's World Title Tournament, rated 6.17.
Looking back to 2021, when Mei Suruga laced up for their first AEW match against Yuka Sakazaki, appearing on AEW Women's World Title Tournament, rated 6.55.
On this day in 2025, Omega & Ospreay touched down in AEW for the first time as a team, appearing on Grand Slam: Australia, rated 8.71 ? a stone-cold classic.
